title: Nursing-home operators the City pays, in the contract screens
question: Do the nursing-home companies Public Health pays also show contracts that grew, ran long or were awarded without bidding?
finding: 5 of the 6 nursing-home operators the City pays by name also appear in the contract screens (growth, no-bid or sole-source): $222.0 million paid in all; 3 of the 5 are confirmed as the operator by their registered address, the rest are name matches. Crestwood Behavioral Health Inc and Helios Healthcare LLC are counted separately here, but their contract notices share a telephone, e-mail domain or officers, so they may be one management. The largest, Crestwood Behavioral Health Inc, was paid $191.1 million; its Public Health agreement grew to $224.2 million (190% over the first approval) and a further $26.3 million contract followed that was not put out to bid (bidding waived by ordinance).
how: Every row of nursing_money "City payments to nursing homes and to the companies they name as related" was looked up, by normalised name, in the published rows of the contract screens (overruns, winners, exceptions, for-profit no-bid, retroactive approvals, record). The amount owed by related companies is the home's own latest State report, from nursing_money "related-balance check", where the home is on that list.
limits: A name match is only a name match. Public Health buys locked mental-health beds and skilled nursing for people it is responsible for; contracts for that care are often waived from bidding by ordinance and lengthened when demand grows, both of which the rules provide for. A balance owed by related companies is a chain's bookkeeping, not a loss. Only the rows each screen publishes are searched.

columns.t: Share of costs paid to related companies (State report)
Owed to a home by related companies
Months added to the end date
Days from registration to a waived-bid contract
